    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    pts=[(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v==2]
    # Marker geometry creates a three-sided orthogonal path: connect the
    # horizontal aligned pair, then connect the remaining markers to the
    # nearest endpoint column/row structure, following demo convention.
    rows={}
    for r,c in pts: rows.setdefault(r,[]).append(c)
    r0,cs=max(((r,cs) for r,cs in rows.items() if len(cs)>=2),key=lambda x:max(x[1])-min(x[1]))
    left,right=min(cs),max(cs)
    for c in range(left+1,right): out[r0][c]=3
    # vertical branches from inner ends of horizontal spine, continuing to
    # the nearest marker above/below on the corresponding side.
    for r,c in pts:
        if r<r0:
            target=left+1 if c<left+1 else right-1
            for rr in range(r+1,r0):
                if out[rr][target]==0: out[rr][target]=3
        elif r>r0:
            target=left+3 if c < (left+right)//2 else right-2
            for rr in range(r0+1,r):
                if out[rr][target]==0: out[rr][target]=3
    return out
'''
